pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
Risk settings before the first trade.
cons: No independent audit of the models.
Broker relationship described vaguely.
Registration details not stated up front.
The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
redFlags: Return claims without verification.
The fee that is not a fee: spreads embedded in every trade.
Restriction lists that name different countries.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.
US$250, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

bottomLine: The verdict on the product is cautious approval: it works, it includes a demo, and it should be used with the minimum deposit while the claims are unproven.
We scored Stream +Opt Celexa 4.0 out of 5. The deductions come from the disclosure gaps, not the mechanics. With the US$250 minimum and the demo as guardrails, the risk stays yours to control.
